overall: An outstanding report: clearly identified ethical issues, balanced and well-evidenced arguments, a defensible decision rule, and stakeholder-specific recommendations. All task requirements are met with strong research and excellent presentation. 50/50.

feedback.summary: An outstanding report that met every task requirement and earned full marks. You identified several ethical issues and linked them to engineering design, built balanced, well-evidenced arguments for and against shipping, and reached a defensible decision rule with stakeholder-specific recommendations. Your research was strong and your presentation excellent. The comments below explain what made each section work and how to sustain this standard.
next_steps: Keep pairing quantitative evidence (e.g., the 81/236 trusts and $4.3B figures) with qualitative case analysis — this combination is what made your arguments so persuasive.
When using analogies like WannaCry, continue explicitly acknowledging their limits (cyberattack vs hardware defect), as you did — this strengthens credibility.
Watch small targets like the ~150-word abstract limit; you were slightly over at ~160 words, which latitude covered here but may not always.

criteria.C1: Excellent work. Your introduction clearly identified several ethical issues — test coverage driven by the release calendar rather than risk, the data-loss rule, and the conflict of interest — and linked each to engineering design. Table 1 tabulating stakeholders, their interests and decision rights demonstrated understanding of both the organisational context and stakeholder interests, the hallmark of the top level.
criteria.C2: Excellent. Your for/against arguments were objective and analytically deepened for this specific contract (e.g., shipping protecting a real competitive advantage), rather than resting on personal opinion. Your conclusions gave distinct decision recommendations for Rachel, management, the health department, the chip supplier and the engineers — exactly the multi-stakeholder consideration the top rubric level requires.
criteria.C3: Excellent. The report's structure — arguments for, arguments against, a decision rule, and the options table — built logically toward your conclusion, so the recommendation followed directly from the evidence. Framing Options B and C as respecting every stakeholder's interests better than either extreme showed systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.
criteria.C4: Excellent research. Eight credible references (NAO, Leveson & Turner, HBR, DOJ, Standards Australia, Engineers Australia) supported your arguments with both quantitative data and qualitative case analysis across four external case studies. Specific figures like the 81 of 236 disrupted hospital trusts and 19,000 cancelled appointments gave your arguments real weight. Maintain this balance of evidence types in future work.
criteria.C5: Excellent presentation. Your writing was fluent and concise, the abstract, introduction, body, conclusion and recommendations each served their function, and you used two tables plus the Figure 1 decision flowchart competently. Your IEEE-style references were consistent and relevant. Note the abstract ran slightly over the ~150-word target; tightening to the stated limit is a good habit for assessments with stricter limits.
